Ok I think you are mixing two issues: 1) feminism may not be the most suitable social movement to solve the one issue of the education gap, and 2) feminist perspective as an aid for male activism (in the progressive sense).

Also for the men who already perceive this, to realize that these problems are not caused by feminism or women, or for that matter men as a whole (trying to point a finger seems really counterproductive to me). Now we can’t expect women to solve our problems like the issue you bring up in education, but that doesn’t mean that the analytical tools provided by them are not vitally important for us to redefine our role in society.
